newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-ARGENTINA BEAT PERU IN FOUL-RIDDEN GAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA BEAT PERU IN FOUL-RIDDEN GAME.

text.p: Argentina, helped by favourable results in other games, moved closer to a place at next year's World Cup finals by beating Peru 2-0 in an often vicious qualifying match on Sunday.
Goals either side of halftime by Hernan Crespo and captain Diego Simeone gave Argentina a comfortable win which lifted them into second place in the single South American group.

Argentina, with 19 points from 11 games, are four points behind leaders Paraguay, who did not play. Peru, with 13 points from 11 games, are eighth, although only one point separates them from fourth-placed Bolivia in an extremly tight group.
Argentina leap-frogged Colombia, who drew 1-1 in Uruguay, and moved further ahead of Bolivia, Ecuador, Uruguay and Chile, who all drew. The top four teams qualify for France next year.

Peru, who scored a shock 1-0 win away to Colombia in their last game, were well-organised tactically and comfortably kept Argentina at bay for much of the first half. They began in lively fashion, creating several chances early on.

But their game plan, where the target was clearly a 0-0 draw, was destroyed in the 44th minute when Claudio Lopez, Argentina's most effective player, crossed from the left and Crespo, unmarked, volleyed the ball home at the far post.
One minute after halftime, Simeone effectively sealed the points when he headed home a cross by Ariel Ortega.
Ortega limped off injured in the 66th minutes after receiving a battering from the Peruvian defence.
Peru never looked like getting back into the game after the second goal and Lopez hit a post near the end.
Argentina, who once again left out star striker Gabriel Batistuta, were often uninspired.

Despite their second place, there has been huge criticism of coach Daniel Passarella, who has chopped and changed the team over the last year. Their results have included defeats against Bolivia and Ecuador and home draws with Paraguay and Chile.
